newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Ramos slams "doomsayers" of Philippine economy.
newsitem.headline: Ramos slams "doomsayers" of Philippine economy.

text.p: Philippine President Fidel Ramos said on Sunday the stability of the peso after its recent weakness proved wrong "doomsayers" who had predicted the country's economic collapse.

"I hope some of those that have been extremely critical... will now examine what they wrote two weeks ago about our economy," Ramos said in a speech to officials in central Cebu city. The text of his speech was released by the presidential palace in Manila.
"I'm sure you will conclude that they were quite wrong in trying to excite people about the coming collapse of the Philippine economy."

"So we are back to reality and I hope that those that criticise just for the sake of opposing the adminsitration will look at their own old files and compare it to the reality now of what is on the ground."

Philippine central bank governor Gabriel Singson said the country's economic fundamentals remained sound and the peso had depreciated by only 6.6 percent after the bank on July 11 allowed it to trade in a wider band. The move followed weeks of speculation in the currency.
Singson said the central bank hoped to make further cuts in its key overnight borrowing rate if the peso, which closed unchanged at 28.000 to the dollar on Friday, continued to stabilise.
He added the rate could return to single digit levels in a few weeks.

The central bank slashed the rate twice last week after the de facto devaluation of the peso. The latest cut on Friday took the rate down to 25 percent. Ahead of last week's reductions, the rate stood at 32 percent.
The problem with Filipinos was "we panic easily," Singson said. "Me, I did not lose sleep because I have seen this too many times in the past."
